reviewed_interpretation: The single authoritative I033 execution is valid and terminal. Fresh target authority, causal anchor/target semantics, coverage gates and exact shipping mirrors all passed. The preregistered relative-delta fidelity hypothesis failed decisively: across 39 benchmarkable causal-anchor cases, median absolute delta error was 6.32364465 dB versus the <=3 dB bound and nearest-rank p90 absolute delta error was 12.9380684 dB versus the <=6 dB bound. Therefore shipping ns_noise_rms_dbfs relative change cannot be promoted as a parameter-free proxy for the later post-NS local observation-domain noise-level change, and no VAD noise-state refresh rule, mapping, threshold or source candidate is selected. Descriptively, shipping NS movement was much smaller than the later local-domain movement: median absolute causal NS delta was 0.4106674 dB versus 6.9787598 dB median absolute future local delta; Pearson correlation was approximately -0.001, Spearman approximately 0.185, and sign agreement was 0.538. These post-hoc diagnostics suggest a state-dynamics/temporal-response mismatch is more informative to test next than another scale or threshold mapping, but they are descriptive only and do not establish a lag or filter candidate.
